method: Read-only .NET ZipArchive decompression, XmlDocument parsing of all top-level XML and relationship parts, SHA256 of decompressed parts, namespace-aware document relationship references, URI-based internal relationship target resolution. Word was not opened or controlled. No DOCX package bytes were modified.

findings.fact: In all nine failures the inserted drawing uses wp:docPr id=1, already used by native ink object name '墨迹 1' inside mc:Choice Requires=wpi. Each baseline has unique docPr identifiers; new drawing insertion introduces the repeated id. The existing ink branch and added drawing can both be active, so these are not mutually exclusive fallback alternatives.
findings.causalStatus: Concrete identifier collision found in all failures. No isolated edit-and-reopen experiment was performed, so this audit does not prove that the collision is the sole cause of Word refusing to open.

findings.fact: All XML/rels examined in the nine failure packages parse; internal relationship targets and referenced r:id/r:embed/r:link values resolve; no duplicate relationship Id or Default extension was found. No original package part is missing and all original word/ink/ink*.xml parts retain identical SHA256. This is not a full OOXML schema validation.

Both baselines already have a 3-column first table whose first row contains two physical w:tc cells, with gridSpan values 2 and 1. First cell contains R1 C1 and R1 C2; second cell contains R1 C3. Edited word/document.xml is byte-identical to baseline in both cases; outer table physical cells remain 8.
findings.interpretation: The first two logical grid columns are already merged before the requested operation. A blanket expected cell-count delta of -1 cannot represent an idempotent merge of those grid columns. UI follow-up should describe the pre-existing merge and lack of a further change; intent to merge the two remaining physical cells would require a different result.
